rationale: Walk-forward on 1.4M rung-observations across 1,871 games, the fitted families are systematically overconfident on long-shot rungs: rungs priced 0.033 settle 0.023, rungs priced 0.072 settle 0.061 (z = -8 to -15, game-clustered). That is a 15-40% relative overstatement, and it lands on exactly the rungs where the market itself overprices long shots -- so an uncorrected pricer reads the market's own long-shot overpricing as an opportunity while being wrong in the same direction, only more so.
features: monotone logit-space recalibration (LadderCalibrator) fitted on the most recent season the model did not train on
target: calibration bias on rungs the model prices below 0.20, and aggregate Brier and log loss on all listed rungs
expected_direction: Bias on p<0.20 rungs shrinks by roughly 75-80% (retrospectively -0.0095 to -0.0018 on targets). Aggregate Brier does NOT measurably improve; log loss improves slightly on the highest-volume statistics. The count of long-shot rungs where the model disagrees with the market in the market's known-wrong direction falls.
test_plan: Prospective on 2026. Price every slate under both shadow-0.3.0 and the calibrated variant, written to the ledger as separate model versions with distinct calibration_version. Pre-specified primary endpoint: calibration bias on settled rungs the raw model priced below 0.20. Secondary: aggregate Brier, expected to be flat -- a large Brier improvement would be evidence something else changed and should be investigated rather than celebrated.
dataset: market-data shadow ledger 2026 + nflverse settled outcomes
result: Retrospective 2020-2025: bias on p<0.20 rungs -0.0077 to -0.0096 raw, -0.0011 to -0.0044 calibrated. Brier flat (+-0.00007), improving in 3/5 statistics. rushing_yards slightly worse on both metrics (0/6 seasons). DIRECTION REVERSES ON THE TRADED POPULATION: fitted to the 2025 Kalshi rungs rather than the fixed synthetic ladder, the model UNDERstates long shots (+0.037 at 0.02-0.05, +0.030 at 0.10-0.20, +0.033 at 0.20-0.35) and OVERstates favourites (-0.041 above 0.70). Applied to a Week-1 snapshot the calibrator raises mean model probability 0.1624 -> 0.1809 and flips disagreements from 114 NO / 20 YES to 77 / 58.
notes: Deliberately NOT deployed into the Week-1 frozen model. The retrospective evidence is real for bias but a wash for aggregate accuracy, and shadow-0.3.0 is frozen; changing it five days before kickoff on that basis is the quiet retuning the freeze exists to prevent. The registered expected direction was derived on a population that is not traded and is now in doubt. Mechanism: shrinkage toward a position prior that is right on average is wrong in both directions on selected subpopulations -- the full ladder contains bench players shrunk upward (overstated long shots), Kalshi lists starters shrunk downward (understated). Arm B must be fitted on the population it is scored on; scripts/shadow/calibrator_two_arm.py now does that. Deployment remains prohibited and the frozen Week-1 arm is untouched.
